purpose: Teach: ときには/何一つ/御飯/もうけ/たずね/そうこう/おみやげ/壊れる

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはときには厳しいことも教えてくださったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father taught me hard things sometimes.
lines.style: Soft, reflective opening. Voice carries the weight of old memory. Measured pace, each phrase deliberate. Gaze turned inward, speaking to the past as much as to her.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、何一つ不平を言われなかったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and you never complained once about it, did you?
lines.style: Warm, knowing affection. A gentle question that's really a confirmation of something she's always understood about him. Slight lift at the end, inviting agreement.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、御飯を子供たちに分けてあげたぞ
lines.en: Gran, back then I shared what rice we had with the other children.
lines.style: Quiet pride in the memory. Voice doesn't rush. There's a steadiness here, not boasting but stating what simply was. Slight pause between thoughts.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、商売のもうけ口をご存知だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you certainly knew where the opportunities were in business, didn't you?
lines.style: Playful acknowledgment, almost teasing him gently. Warm underneath. She's calling out his capability without letting him hide behind modesty. Light, knowing tone.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、村人がお家をたずねてきたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, people from the village would come to our home.
lines.style: Reflective, almost wondering. The memory of being needed, of doors opening. Voice steady but soft, like he's tracing the outline of something precious and distant.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、そうこうしてるうちに歳をとったとお笑いだったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And all that time passing, you'd laugh about how we'd grown old before we knew it.
lines.style: Tender recognition of shared time. There's love and a little rueful humor in this. She's saying: I remember you noticing, I remember you laughing. Voice warm, intimate, like a private understanding between them.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんからおみやげを頂いて嬉しかったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when I was young, Father gave me souvenirs and I was so happy.
lines.style: The softest moment yet. Voice almost fragile with the depth of gratitude and affection. Slow. The happiness isn't bright—it's deep, settled, borne across decades.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、形あるものは壊れると、おっしゃってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you always used to say that things with form eventually break, didn't you?
lines.style: Close, intimate murmur. She's finishing his thought, the way long-married people do. Tender but with quiet wisdom underneath. She's reminding him—and herself—of what lasts.
